prompt: Merge two parts at each step, from singletons to $\{V(G)\}$. Join distinct parts by a red edge exactly when their original adjacency is neither complete nor empty. Minimise the largest red degree over the entire sequence. Which parameter is this?

answers.explanation: Red edges record non-homogeneous pairs of parts. The width is a maximum degree over all intermediate red graphs, minimised over binary merge sequences.
Clique-width minimises labels in a graph-building expression, not red degree during contractions.
Treewidth uses bags in a tree decomposition; it is not defined by this merging process.
Shrubdepth concerns bounded-height, bounded-colour tree-models for a class.
Rank-width minimises the maximum binary rank of adjacency matrices across decomposition cuts.
Neighbourhood diversity counts twin classes in one partition; it does not optimise an entire contraction sequence.
Merge-width counts parts reached through resolved pairs of original vertices, not red degree between current parts.
Component twin-width bounds the size of red connected components, rather than their maximum degree.
Linear clique-width restricts labelled construction expressions to adding one vertex at a time.
That parameter counts reachable parts in resolved-pair components and is equivalent in boundedness to clique-width.

sources.title: Bonnet et al. — Twin-width I, §§2–4 (2021 version)
Dreier & Toruńczyk — Merge-width and First-Order Model Checking, Definitions 3.1–3.2 and §7 (June 2026 version)
